newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-BRUGUERA CRUISES BUT COURIER STRUGGLES IN MONTE CARLO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BRUGUERA CRUISES BUT COURIER STRUGGLES IN MONTE CARLO.

text.p: Jim Courier and Sergi Bruguera, who are fighting hard to restore their past pride on clay, both made it to the second round of the Monte Carlo tennis Open on Monday.
But of the two former French Open winners, the American, seeded 13, had by far the harder first round, needing three hardfought sets to get through against Slovakia's Dominik Hrbaty -- 6-7 7-5 6-4.
Bruguera, winner here in 1991 and 1993, dismissed fellow Spaniard Javier Sanchez 6-4 6-1.
"It was the first time I met him and he's a very talented young player," said Courier, who was playing his first ATP Tour match on clay this season.

"The first match on clay is always difficult. I'm very happy to have come through this especially as the conditions were difficult. It was very windy out there," the 1991 and 1992 French Open champion added.
Courier had a good start, leading 4-1 into the match before his game started to falter. The 19-year-old Hrbaty, ranked 60th in the world, made it back to 5-5 and went on to win the tie break 7-1.
The second set was undecided until the 11th game, when Courier took the upper hand and broke his opponent at last to win the set 7-5.

Things went much more smoothly for the American in the final set until he had to serve for the match with a 5-2 30-15 lead. Two double faults and an unforced error earned Hrbaty a reprieve but he eventually bowed 6-4 after two hours and 28 minutes.
Bruguera had a far easier task, spending half as much time on court as Courier but he said he still found it hard to adapt to the slow surface after months on hardcourt.
"It is very hard to be patient enough, to get the right discipline on clay. You always want to finish points quickly," he said to explain a pedestrian start to the game.
The 1993 and 1994 French Open champion, seeded 16th, trailed Sanchez 2-0 at first but soon recovered to level at 3-3 and win the first set at the net.
The second set was a tennis lesson as Bruguera outpaced his rival to hand him his third defeat in this third clash between the two Spaniards this season.
"There must be 18 or 19 of us on the circuit so it is only natural that we should meet often between Spaniards," said Bruguera, whose game suffered last season following an operation.
Spaniards will be among the favourites in this year's Monte Carlo tournament with 12 of them in the draw, half of them seeds. Four Spaniards played the semifinals of the Barcelona Open last week.
Bruguera, who surged back in Key Biscaine this season, losing only in the final to Austrian Thomas Muster, hopes he will be the one who makes the best impression here.
"I've worked very hard to be back at my best after the worst season of my career. Hopefully, this season I will play as well as in the past," he said.
